`class BorderNodeEffect`<br/>
**Extends:** [`NodeEffect<Node>`](/reference/effects/nodeeffect/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.ui.node.effect.impl` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [BorderNodeEffect.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/ui/node/effect/impl/BorderNodeEffect.java)

Outlines the pixels that a node draws, outside or inside their edge.

![A white rectangle with a thick grey border](/captures/catalog-effects-bordernodeeffect.webp)

## Description

The outline follows the drawn shape, not the bounds: rounded corners, a disc, glyphs, the opaque part of an image.
A gradient [`Color`](/reference/drawing/color/) runs across the bounds of the node.
Its priority is `200`, so it outlines the result of the rounded, circle and blur passes, whatever the order you add them in.
The border setters of a [`RectNode`](/reference/nodes/rectnode/) drive the `BorderNodeEffect` of the node: give a rectangle one or the other.

## Property details

<a id="BorderNodeEffect-property-color"></a>

### color

- `this color(Color color)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `this color(Supplier<Color> colorSupplier)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">signal</span>
- `this color(Function<N,Color> colorFunction)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Color of the border.
The overload that takes a `Function` receives the node, so that the color can depend on its state, such as its focus.
